evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We run a savings product for casual workers around Kampala: porters, construction laborers, boda riders. The ask is chosen: an agent offers, in person at the work site, to open a named savings wallet and take a first deposit. Opening is free, takes ten minutes, and can be done any day an agent is there. In interviews nearly all workers said they want to save for school fees and mean to start 'next week'; when our agents visit, mostly on Tuesdays, people say they have nothing on them. Porters and laborers are paid in cash on Friday afternoons; boda riders earn daily. Rent is due at month start; school fees fall in early February, late May, and early September; Christmas is the big spending season. A colleague wants to launch in the first week of January as a 'new year, new start' campaign. When should the agent make the offer?
evals.expected_output: A choice of moment in the output template that ties the offer to when wages are paid and does not adopt the new-year launch.
assertions: Every row of the money calendar comes from what the user said or is marked assumed.
Tests the program's current Tuesday visit and at least two other moments on money, attention, and whether the action can be done.
Chooses a moment tied to Friday wages, names money in hand as what it relies on, and promises no effect size for this program.
Rejects the first week of January or marks it untested, noting the spending around it.
Names who the chosen moment leaves out, such as riders who earn daily, and gives them a second moment.
Ends with two or three next moves, each with its reason, and questions the user could ask next, with no single instruction.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: When is the best time to send our message?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks what the ask is, what shows the moment is the barrier, when money comes in and goes out, and when the action can be done, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks what people are being asked to do and what it costs them at that moment.
Asks when money comes in and goes out for these people.
Asks when the action can be done.
Does not choose a moment or fill in a calendar from general knowledge of any country.
Says why it needs these answers.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We're a microfinance institution in western Kenya. We want to time our input-loan offer (seed and fertilizer on credit, repaid after the next harvest) to land right after the maize harvest in August, when farmers have cash and feel optimistic. In our survey of 300 smallholders, 70% said they want to use fertilizer and that by planting in March the harvest money is gone. Loan officers can visit any week and dealers stock inputs all year. School fees fall in January, May, and September, and many farmers already carry a school-fees loan. Tell us the exact timing.
evals.expected_output: The skill specifies the moment and says a consumer-protection specialist must check affordability and disclosure before any pilot because the ask is a loan timed to when farmers hold the most cash.
assertions: Names a consumer-protection or financial-inclusion specialist to review the offer before any pilot.
Says what to bring to that specialist.
Names farmers who already carry a school-fees loan as people the chosen moment could leave worse off.
Does not present the timing as ready to launch without that review.
Does not quote an effect size from the Kenyan fertilizer study as what the loan offer will achieve.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We've decided to make the fertilizer offer in the two weeks after harvest. Now: how many SMS reminders should go out before the deadline, at what spacing, and should the last one be the day before?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the moment is already chosen and the question is the number and spacing of reminders, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the question is how many reminders and how often, not which moment.
